prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE exceptionally polished ORIGINAL high-end desktop food ordering website screenshot for fictional brand SUPPER. This is a flat raster UI design study, NOT a presentation board or device mockup, no surrounding labels. Full scrolling desktop webpage, portrait canvas about 1536 x 2048, wide desktop layout with fine crisp readable UI. Functional inspiration: restaurant menu browsing from DoorDash, but completely original branding, page composition, type, food photography and details. Brand: small beautiful wordmark 'supper' in expressive editorial serif; deep aubergine #422B39 ink/buttons, warm apricot #EFAD8E accents, warm ivory #FAF7F2 canvas. Display headings refined contemporary serif; all body/UI clean humanist sans. Generous whitespace, thin dividers, very restrained rounded rectangles, superb typography. Header wordmark at left, understated search centrally, 'Brooklyn' and 'Basket 0' right. Thin flow line '01 Choose a meal — 02 Customize — 03 Review — 04 Confirm'. Main desktop content uses a compact left category rail, large airy central menu and a slim right delivery summary. Main heading 'Sunday Table' with small 'Seasonal comfort food, made nearby.' and '25–35 min · Delivery $2.99'. Wide shallow original editorial photography of seasonal roasted vegetables and ceramic dishes. Below, 'Made for tonight' section with a 3-column grid of six beautifully photographed meals on uncluttered ivory surfaces: Harvest bowl $18, Lemon chicken $22, Roasted cauliflower $19, Green goddess salad $17, Wild mushroom pasta $24, Citrus salmon $26. Every card only food photo, one short title, one supporting line, price and a neat add circle; no competing badges or overlays. Right small summary shows delivery timeframe and 'Your basket is empty' plus one clear invitation to choose a meal. Lower down a calm 'A little something extra' row of 3 side dishes and 'From the kitchen' story strip with one small kitchen photo, then compact footer. No giant marketing hero, no dashboards, no copied logos, no actual brand names, no lorem ipsum, no browser chrome, no phone or tablet. Desktop columns remain desktop all the way down. Complete page top to footer with consistent spacing. Photoreal appetizing real food. Make this genuinely art-directed and production-quality with detailed but calm UI. Text legible, spell Supper correctly.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE ORIGINAL luxury-quality desktop grocery ordering website screenshot for fictional brand FIELDWORK, a complete scrolling desktop webpage top to footer. Flat UI artwork, no device, no presentation margins or captions. Portrait canvas about 1536 x 2048 but the website itself has a wide desktop layout. Strong functional inspiration from Instacart: grocery search, store identity, departments, product add controls and visible delivery context. Invent a distinct composition and brand identity, do not copy Instacart graphics, green palette, carrot logo or typography. FIELDWORK brand uses deep petrol ink #173C4B, butter yellow #F2CE67, chalk ivory #FBF9F3. Friendly round geometric sans display type and very legible neutral sans interface. Small typographic 'fieldwork' logo with an original tiny four-square sprout-like abstract mark. Very airy, restrained, editorial, beautifully detailed real grocery photography. Top header has logo, search 'Find something good', delivery area 'Brooklyn', basket icon '0'. Thin process '01 Shop — 02 Basket — 03 Delivery — 04 Confirm'. Main header 'Neighborhood Market' with 'Good food. Close to home.' and small delivery slot chip 'Today, 4–5 pm'. No giant marketing hero. A narrow left department list Produce, Dairy & eggs, Bakery, Pantry, Frozen. Main shopping content starts with a quiet shallow still-life banner of fresh produce, then department tabs and 'Fresh this week'. Show 8 product cards in two rows of four: Organic bananas $1.49 / bunch; Strawberries $5.00 / 1 lb; Avocados $2.00 / each; Garden tomatoes $3.50 / 1 lb; Oat milk $4.50 / 32 fl oz; Sourdough $7.00 / loaf; Farm eggs $6.00 / dozen; Greek yogurt $4.00 / 16 oz. Each product sits on a clean neutral background with precise pack quantity, price, one name, and a single petrol plus-circle aligned bottom right. One item has a tidy inline quantity control instead of plus. Small right-hand basket rail with 3 item miniatures and subtotal $13.99 plus 'Review basket' but not loud. Below a 'Pantry, considered' collection of 4 products then small market story and quiet footer. Ample whitespace around every zone; no promos competing with food, no chat bubbles, no sale ribbons. Keep every interface element original, realistically usable, precisely aligned and high resolution. All text concise and correctly spelled. This is an ordering interface, not a generic landing page.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE ORIGINAL premium desktop flight-search and comparison website screenshot for fictional travel brand WAYFAR. Full scrolling desktop page top to footer, flat raster UI image, portrait canvas about 1536 x 2048 containing a wide desktop interface. Functional inspiration from KAYAK's flight comparison and fare clarity, but no copied branding, orange tiles, layout details or real airline logos. Original brand: geometric lowercase wordmark 'wayfar' with subtle small directional glyph. Indigo #333F87, soft mint #BCE3D4, ice #F3F6FC, white. Precise contemporary geometric sans, clean typography with tabular numerals. Airy sophisticated travel product, minimal badges, no ads. Header wordmark, Flights / Stays / Trips nav, support, account. Compact search strip 'New York JFK' to 'London LHR', 'Nov 12 — Nov 19', '1 adult · Economy', indigo 'Search flights'. Progress line '01 Compare — 02 Choose a fare — 03 Traveler — 04 Confirm'. Main heading 'New York to London' with quiet date subheading. Left narrow filter rail contains stops, departure time, bags, airlines, with generous separated sections. Main area has 3 understated sort tabs 'Recommended $815', 'Lowest price $792', 'Fastest 7h 05m'. Four large wide itinerary rows with clear aligned outbound and return times, duration, stops, two baggage glyphs and total round-trip price, plus one 'View fare' button. Fictional carriers Atlas Air, Northstar, Meridian, no actual airline logos. Selected row Atlas Air, departure 8:05 am JFK to 8:05 pm LHR, nonstop 7h; return 10:10 am LHR to 1:10 pm JFK, nonstop 8h; $815 round trip. Other prices $846, $892, $928. Use an original elegant line for flight itinerary, not decorative illustrations. A slim right companion panel 'Your trip, at a glance' route / dates / traveler, plus tasteful small monochrome London photo; keep area calm. Lower section 'A little flexibility goes a long way' includes a compact week-price strip and brief baggage/fare comparison then footer. Finish as coherent full webpage. Avoid big marketing imagery, giant blank areas, ads, clutter, fake app store promo frames, charts unrelated to travel, tiny unreadable text, copied UI. Show a highly detailed, realistic production-ready booking comparison design.

Use case: ui-mockup. Create ONE ORIGINAL high-end desktop hotel booking comparison website screenshot for fictional brand STILLHOUSE. A complete scrolling desktop results page top to footer, flat raster UI artwork, no device chrome, no presentation labels. Portrait canvas approximately 1536 x 2048 with a wide desktop layout. Functional influence Booking.com: destination/date/guest search, hotel comparison, clear nightly/stay prices, room availability CTA. Design an original elegant boutique-travel visual identity, never copy Booking.com's blue/yellow branding or dense styling. STILLHOUSE logo beautiful understated editorial serif, pine #183E36 primary ink and buttons, muted clay #CE8D76 accent, warm cream #FAF8F1 background. High-contrast contemporary serif headings with clean humanist sans interface. Luxury editorial restraint, very airy spacing, warm natural original interior photos. Header logo, Stays / Collections / Your trips, account. Search strip 'London' 'Nov 12 — Nov 19' '2 adults · 1 room' and pine 'Find a stay'. Subtle progress '01 Find a stay — 02 Room & rate — 03 Your details — 04 Confirm'. Main heading 'Stay a little closer.' with 'London · 7 nights · 2 guests'. Left narrow filter rail Neighbourhood / Nightly budget / Stay style / Essentials, small map thumbnail. Main column 3 or 4 generous horizontal property cards. Cards have large tasteful room photographs at left; at right property name, neighborhood, small score, one description, then nightly and total clearly separated plus one 'View rooms' action. Original properties The Alder House (Bloomsbury, 9.4, $240 / night, $1,680 for 7 nights), Rowan & Stone (Marylebone, 9.2, $265 / night, $1,855 stay), The Marlow (Fitzrovia, 9.1, $220 / night, $1,540 stay). Photographs use sunlight, oak, natural textiles and rich design detail. No starbadge clutter or urgency banners. Subtle save heart sits outside photo with enough room. Lower content concise area guide for Bloomsbury, Marylebone and Fitzrovia with three small editorial neighborhood images, then footer. Keep search/results primary; avoid a giant destination marketing hero. Exact names and prices legible; clean whitespace, calibrated serif sizes, unusually good typography and very convincing responsive desktop UI. Show the complete page with intentional alignment and a clear forward path.
